rv.q: This odd little show has charm aplenty, though for some it may also prove something of a well-intentioned dog's dinner.
Giving human voices to pets was something of a double-edged sword in this case.

We meet Sarita (Vinita Belani) on the first day of her divorced life, as she relocates from suburbia to a New York tenement. Downsized and downtrodden, she stumbles upon a stray dog intent on befriending her. Sarita insists she is not a dog person, but she is a nice person, so she reluctantly agrees to foster the nameless mutt.
By taking itself a touch too seriously, “Dog Mom” weakens the messages that are better served with humour.
Well meaning canine comedy goes astray.

cn.t: Critics find this canine comedy well-meaning but misguided, with its premise of actors playing talking dogs failing to deliver consistent laughs despite tapping into pet-owner culture.
